reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes earning money through a Forsage BUSD refer-and-earn system and links daily earnings to recruiting others. The speaker asks participants to invite 200–300 people and message their groups, while associating results within about 30 days with system promotion and related activities. The material does not establish actual earnings or transaction outcomes, and the instruction not to cheat anyone does not verify the earnings claims.

citations.quote: EARN MONEY WITH FORSAGE BUSD
It's a reference system of a refer and earn.
if we can promote our system, we will get daily earnings on the daily basis.
when you bring someone to your business, it doesn't matter what the other person says. You must take the responsibility of minding them properly.
You have earned a lot because you have listened to the system your new upline.

opening.argument: The presentation includes meaningful risk qualifications rather than an unconditional promise. It expressly says cryptocurrency is unstable and can move up or down, and describes trading as high risk on both sides. The discussion also distinguishes the referral model from trading and mining, presenting the material as an explanation of different approaches rather than a guarantee that every participant will profit. Those qualifications make the content more consistent with an informed business training session than deceptive solicitation.

citations.quote: It is unstable.
This can be the high risk of both the sides.
Our forex is no trading or mining.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The title's phrase about earning money identifies the subject, but does not itself establish a false guarantee. The cited referral language shows an invitation to share a system, while the surrounding material expressly discusses volatility and risk. The statement about results within 30 days is also not defined as a guaranteed financial return; the excerpt does not specify what “result” means.

citations.quote: EARN MONEY WITH FORSAGE BUSD
if we can promote our system, we will get daily earnings on the daily basis.
It is unstable.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The risk discussion is directed to cryptocurrency trading, not to the promoted referral opportunity. The presentation separately says that promotion can produce daily earnings and calls the model “refer and earn.” Thus, volatility language about other methods does not qualify the central recruitment-linked earnings message.

citations.quote: This can be the high risk of both the sides.
if we can promote our system, we will get daily earnings on the daily basis.
It's a reference system of a refer and earn.

opening.argument: The supplied description calls this a training session, and the presentation spends substantial time explaining cryptocurrency concepts, exchange functions, volatility, trading, mining, and referral methods. It discusses the costs and operational demands of mining and contrasts them with the stated referral model. That structure is instructional: viewers are being taught how the presenter characterizes several crypto activities, not shown proof of a completed transaction or an assured outcome.

This is the refer and earn business, you don't need any money

rebuttal.rebuttal: The request to invite participants occurs inside the training format and does not by itself prove that the entire session is a scam. The 200–300 figure is an instruction to invite people to a session, while the financial mechanism, if any, is not demonstrated through a transaction, account record, or verified payout. The reference account therefore overstates what the instructional excerpts establish.

citations.quote: I want to invite ma'am in the form of 200-300 participants
TRAINING SESSION
Where you get a knowledge and share it and share for it

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Calling the event training does not change what the lesson tells participants to do. The material explicitly says to promote the system for daily earnings and to bring someone into the business. Teaching recruitment as the route to earnings is still promotional conduct, even when presented as education and without a displayed payout.

citations.quote: if we can promote our system, we will get daily earnings on the daily basis.
when you bring someone to your business

opening.argument: The presentation describes a referral-based business service and expressly distinguishes it from trading and mining. It says participants share knowledge through a system and states that they do not need money for that referral activity. The supplied excerpts do not identify a required deposit, a guaranteed return, a credential request, or a defined tiered payout formula. A referral invitation may be commercially promotional without establishing a fraudulent mechanism.

citations.quote: Our forex is no trading or mining.
This is the refer and earn business, you don't need any money
Don't cheat anyone right now.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The existence of referral promotion does not automatically establish fraud. The cited material identifies sharing and bringing people into a business, but it does not state that participants must pay a deposit or receive a fixed return. The instruction not to cheat anyone is relevant context, and the excerpts do not show a completed transaction or an actual victim.

Don't cheat anyone right now.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The absence of a displayed deposit does not resolve the central issue. The presentation ties earnings to promoting the system, asks participants to bring others into the business, and explicitly calls the arrangement “refer and earn.” Those statements describe recruitment-linked compensation even if the excerpt does not disclose the precise payment terms.
